title: The TCP/IP model and how it maps onto OSI

videos.script: Lesson 1 drew seven layers. The internet runs on a model with four. It came from the people who built the protocols, and it describes what they built rather than what a committee hoped for. {{four}} The difference is not only a count. The four layers match who does the work on a real computer. The program speaks its protocol. The kernel does TCP, IP and routing. The network card and its driver put bits on the wire. {{who}} In this lesson you will watch a program hand its work to the kernel, one system call at a time. Then you will follow a single ping across the office router and see what the router changes and what it leaves alone. {{hop}} The office has one public address, and every machine inside borrows it. You will see that on the web server's log. {{nat}} And you will meet a fault that confuses support for days: small pages load, large ones hang. It comes from a limit on packet size and a message somebody blocked. You will break it on purpose, and then fix it the way routers do. {{mtu}}
